text:
maya: Heads up — on the 8k long-context load test with continuous batching on, I'm seeing steady KV cache growth until OOM. Repro in staging.

jon: Can you paste the flamegraph/allocs and the exact loadtest flags?

maya: Sure. Quick snapshot from staging:
```
MEM: kv_fragments: 2.1G -> 6.8G over 45m
Pinned fragments count: 18k -> 64k
Eviction attempts: frequent, but reclaim rate ~0
Batch merges/sec spikes at ~1200
Latency p50 token gen: 34ms -> 78ms
```
Load command: `./loadtest --seq-len=8192 --threads=96 --continuous-batching=merge_split --batch-window=6ms --kv-eager-evict=false`

lee: That pattern smells like head-of-line blocking during batch merge. If a merged batch contains one request with huge KV accesses, the whole batch holds the KV pages and pins fragments until completion. Eviction can't make progress.

ash: Also note kernel selection: for seq > 4096 we switch to the slow NCHW kernel path on A100 which increases per-token time by ~2x. That increases batch duration and the chance of merges overlapping with eviction windows.

perf-bot: Regression alert: change set `runtime/batch: adjust merge heuristics` (2026-03-15) correlated with +30% kv pinned time in canary.

jon: Two-pronged investigation: (1) try avoiding merges that mix long-context requests with short ones; (2) add backpressure to prevent large merged batches from pinning too many fragments.

maya: I ran a quick experiment: forcing `--continuous-batching=split-by-seqlen` reduced peak pinned fragments from 64k -> 9k and memory stable. But throughput dropped ~12%.

ash: That's expected. Patch idea: when merging, check per-shard pinned_count + projected_fragments > threshold => abort merge. Pseudo: `if (shard.pinned_estimate + merge_estimated_fragments > MAX_PINNED) return split();`

lee: + also consider a fast path kernel selection hint: if merge would contain a request >4k, tag batch and force early split to use the slow kernel in its own queue so it doesn't penalize others. 

jon: Good. Can we add a telemetry gauge for "merge_aborted_reason=kv_pin_threshold" and a percentile for per-merge projected_fragments? Need to see distribution.

maya: I'll add the telemetry and run another canary with `--batch-window=3ms` and the merge-abort patch. I'll attach flamegraphs.

ash: One more: eviction currently ignores fragments with recently-chosen kernels because they're being used by the execution thread. Maybe we can opportunistically decrement a fragment's "recently_active" counter if it's blocking eviction longer than X ms. Might help reclamation.

lee: Risky but plausible. Implementation detail: decrement only if fragment not referenced in last N tokens and eviction queue backlog > Y.

jon: Action items: maya to roll merge-abort patch + telemetry to staging; lee to prototype kernel-tagging split; ash to put up a short doc on kernel path timings and thresholds. We'll reconvene after canary results.

maya: Thanks — starting the canary now. Will drop the flamegraphs here in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
